subject: mathematics
title: Equivalent fractions
summary: Different-looking fractions that are the same amount, and how to simplify them.

lesson.text: A fraction is part of a whole. In 3/4, the bottom number (the denominator) tells us the whole is cut into 4 equal parts, and the top number (the numerator) tells us we have 3 of them.

Cut a loaf of bread into 2 equal pieces and take 1: that is 1/2. Cut the same loaf into 4 equal pieces and take 2: that is 2/4. You have the same amount of bread. So 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent fractions.
Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number. The fraction stays the same amount.

lesson.title: Fill the gap: 2/5 = ?/10
steps: Do the same to the top: 2 × 2 = 4.

lesson.text: To simplify, divide the top and the bottom by the same number until no number except 1 divides both.

lesson.title: Simplify 6/8
steps: Nothing except 1 divides both 3 and 4, so 3/4 is the simplest form.

lesson.text: Whatever you do to the top, do to the bottom. If you multiply only one of them, the amount changes.

questions.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom of 1/2 by 3: (1 × 3)/(2 × 3) = 3/6.
5 × 2 = 10, so multiply the top by 2 as well: 2 × 2 = 4. So 2/5 = 4/10.

questions.prompt: What is 6/8 in its simplest form?
questions.explanation: Divide the top and bottom by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4, giving 3/4. Nothing else divides both 3 and 4.

questions.prompt: Which fraction is NOT equal to 2/3?
questions.explanation: 4/6, 6/9 and 8/12 all simplify to 2/3. 3/4 is a different amount: three quarters is more than two thirds.

questions.prompt: Ada ate 2/8 of a cake. What is 2/8 in its simplest form?
questions.explanation: Divide the top and bottom by 2: 2 ÷ 2 = 1 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Ada ate 1/4 of the cake.
